evidence.label: derived
evidence.claim: Cosmos and Center share the contracts/wire boundary. The Pin runtime does not: pin/runtime/core/build.rs compiles a second, independently authored copy of the same stock packages, so the workspace holds two wire trees that answer the same RPC paths. contracts/wire-divergence.json is the inventory of where they disagree, and the divergenceGate above is what now holds both trees to it: it parses each one and fails when they encode a shared field number differently anywhere the inventory does not already record.

evidence.label: implemented
evidence.claim: Cosmos serves, and Center's server-side adapter loads, the independently authored schemas in contracts/wire. Pin is deliberately not listed: no code under pin/ compiles this artifact.

evidence.label: derived
evidence.claim: The device runtime compiles its own copy of the stock packages and serves the same RPC paths over loopback. It disagrees with contracts/wire on 95 inventoried points, NONE of which change the bytes: the last two - humane.provisioning.VerifyHmcAssociationRequest fields 1 and 2 - were settled on 2026-08-12 from the stock client's own decompiled class, which declares hmc_id at 1 and the verification signature at 2, and the pin tree was corrected onto that layout. The two trees are compared by the build: platform/deploy/acceptance/wire-equivalence.test.mjs parses both, fails when the set of field numbers they encode differently is anything other than the inventoried list (today, empty), and since 2026-08-12 also fails when any inventory entry stops describing what the trees actually declare. See contracts/wire-divergence.json.
evidence.labelRationale: Stays `derived` on 2026-08-12 after the last two byte-changing divergences were settled. `observed` would be the upgrade the settlement does NOT buy: the evidence is the client's generated class read off an artifact, not a stock client watched exercising these paths on loopback, and two of the corrections are not yet on the device at all. `implemented` would still be a DOWNGRADE in information - it would assert the runtime serves the tree, which was never in doubt, while saying nothing about the fidelity that was. `derived` is what this file uses for a typed, source-grounded statement containing its explicit unknowns without asserting physical-device acceptance, and that is exactly what the inventory plus the equivalence gate are.
evidence.residualRisk: Not a divergence between the trees any more - that inventory is byte-clean - but a gap between the tree and the DEVICE. Two corrections change what the Pin puts on the wire and are staged rather than installed: humane.capture.DeleteMemoryStatus, where the store-error arm of Capture.DeleteMemory moves from 3 to 4 (until then a stock client is told a failed delete was refused for authorization, while Cosmos answers 4 for the same outcome), and humane.provisioning.VerifyHmcAssociationRequest, where a stock pairing call currently fails to decode. Both are recorded under `stagedForRelease` in contracts/wire-divergence.json with what changes and what to check on install, held there by the equivalence gate, and written up in README.md#connect-a-pin. They clear when a Pin release containing them is installed and the checks are run.
